findings.owner_decision: option (a) - wire cancellation reusing the existing cancel-frame / bounded-grace / terminate_preserving retirement machinery

wiring: src/backend.rs:219-253 dispatch_with_cancellation: tokio::select! over reply.closed() and state.shutdown.cancelled() fires a caller-owned CancellationToken; the pinned dispatch future is then awaited to completion (not dropped) so the retirement sequence - cooperative cancel frame, bounded grace, terminate_preserving, tree reaping - runs to completion; the code comment documents why dropping would kill the worker without reclaiming its process tree or request temp directory

src/backend.rs:134-141: pre-dispatch check is now state.shutdown.is_cancelled() || reply.is_closed(), mirroring src/supervisor.rs:186 - both concrete consequences from the round-1 finding (cancellation unobserved; unreachable pre-dispatch branch) are addressed
src/resident_worker.rs:286-331 run_request: select! races the caller cancellation against the dispatch; the Cancelled arm routes to retire_cancelled

src/resident_worker.rs:362-379 retire_cancelled: marks unhealthy, reuses cancel_active_request (cooperative frame + CANCELLATION_GRACE) and terminate_preserving; on clean containment reports the CLI-shaped interrupted response (RunResponse exit_code -1); a containment failure surfaces WORKER_TERMINATION_FAILURE instead of a false success

src/resident_worker_manager.rs:94-107 execute_with_cancellation: the trigger is passed through the exclusive lease to the leased worker, so a request blocked on execution_gate cannot be cancelled without touching the active worker
Cargo.toml:19 adds tokio-util 0.7 (rt feature) for the cancellation token; Cargo.lock already contains it as a transitive dep, no new transitive tree
tests: tests/resident_backend.rs:199 resident_backend_client_cancellation_retires_the_active_worker: spawns the real executor with a 120s request on the new equest-slow fixture (tests/fixtures/resident_worker_runtime.py, sleeps 120s and does not read frames while executing), waits for manager status Busy, aborts the handler task (closing the reply channel exactly like a client disconnect), then asserts within 20s that the worker is retired (status Empty), that the admission permit is released, and that the owned per-request temp directory is reclaimed
ran the test twice more in isolation plus once in the full cargo test run: 3/3 passes, no observed flakiness

the test directly exercises the round-1 acceptance criterion: slow fixture request + dropped client, and proves the cancelled request does NOT run to its deadline (a miss would take >=120s against the 20s assertion window and would leave the worker Busy)
verification.design_5_conformance: Design section 5 sequence implemented: cooperative cancel frame sent for the active request (request-ID matched), completion cannot be proven for a frame-blind executing worker, so within the bounded grace the whole worker is terminated and replaced for the next request - the known cost (retiring a healthy warm worker) is explicitly accepted in owner-decisions.md and will shrink with the bounded pool (11-04)

success_is_an_identical_run_response_on_both_backends: same args through the CLI supervisor (python binary + [script, success]) and the real resident worker; asserts 200 on both and byte-identical bodies {exit_code:0, stdout:"contract stdout\n", stderr:"contract stderr\n"}, worker stays Ready, no owned temp residue on either side

timeout_diverges_exactly_as_the_owner_approved: same hang fixture args; CLI asserts the documented 200/exit_code:-1 shape (with a ready-marker wait so the deadline does not race process startup, and temp reclamation asserted); resident asserts 500 WORKER_TIMEOUT with a non-empty diagnostic, worker retired to Empty, no residue - exactly the approved divergence, referenced to owner-decisions.md in the test doc comment

business_error_shapes_diverge_exactly_as_the_owner_approved: unstructured failure (exit 1) is byte-identical on both backends; the resident-only structured channel asserts 500 + verbatim FIXTURE_FAILURE with the worker kept Ready - the lossy CLI shape the owner approved replacing is asserted as the baseline
verification.traceability: tests/backend_contract.rs header and each divergence test name/comment reference .trellis/tasks/11-03-resident-worker-runtime-upgrade/review/owner-decisions.md, so the approved API change is traceable from code as required by the decision's scope
verification.no_behavior_change: the diff adds no source change to the error-mapping path; it only records and tests the existing shapes (verified: src/executor.rs and src/supervisor.rs are untouched by this diff)

new_issues_examined: Cancellation response shape: a cancelled client receives 200/exit_code:-1 (retire_cancelled returns the CLI-shaped interrupted RunResponse) rather than the 503 the round-1 recommendation text sketched - this is the CLI-consistent shape (src/supervisor.rs documents the HTTP timeout/cancel response as 200 exit_code -1) and matches the owner decision's "consistent with the CLI" requirement, so it is not a finding

retire_cancelled only suppresses WORKER_CANCELLED on the success path; a containment failure surfaces WORKER_TERMINATION_FAILURE, so a cancelled request never falsely reports success with a live worker

dispatch_with_cancellation pins the dispatch future and awaits it after the trigger fires; temp settlement happens inside the awaited future (RequestTemp.settle) before the permit is released, so no cleanup or permit leak on the cancellation path (also asserted by the test's permit + temp-dir claims)
biased select! ordering (cancel checked first) is correct: if both are ready the request is treated as cancelled, which retires and replaces the worker - safe for correctness
contract_echo.py hang-mode ready marker is written into the owned request dir via TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP, which both backends export - deterministic cross-backend synchronization
tokio-util is already present in Cargo.lock transitively; adding it as a direct dependency changes no dependency tree

no regression surface: the timeout/protocol/EOF retirement paths were refactored from inline code into dispatch() + Dispatched enum but are behavior-identical (same codes, same retire set: protocol failure, output limit, deadline); all round-1 resident_worker/resident_worker_manager tests still pass unchanged
